provider_guide.npm.step_1.title: Create a dedicated NPM user
provider_guide.npm.step_1.body:
Vauxtra needs a user account in Nginx Proxy Manager to manage proxy hosts.

1. Open NPM at http://<npm-host>:81
2. Go to Users (top-right menu) → Add User
3. Fill in name, email and a strong password
4. Under Permissions, enable Manage Proxy Hosts
5. Save — then use that email and password in the next step

Tip: Using a dedicated Vauxtra user (instead of admin) limits blast radius.
provider_guide.npm.step_2.title: Enter the NPM URL
provider_guide.npm.step_2.body: Enter the URL of your NPM admin panel. The default port is 81.
provider_guide.npm.step_2.url.label: NPM URL
provider_guide.npm.step_2.url.hint: Use the internal IP or hostname. Include the port (default: 81).
provider_guide.npm.step_3.title: NPM Credentials
provider_guide.npm.step_3.body: Enter the email and password of the NPM user you created in step 1.
provider_guide.npm.step_3.username.label: Email
provider_guide.npm.step_3.username.hint: The email you set when creating the NPM user.
provider_guide.npm.step_3.password.label: Password
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_1.title: Prepare the Zoraxy web console
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_1.body:
Vauxtra logs in to the Zoraxy web console with the same username and password you use in the browser, then manages proxy rules and reads certificates through its API.

Zoraxy has a single administrator account: Vauxtra will use it, so keep the console (port 8000) on your LAN or VPN and never expose it publicly.

If Zoraxy runs with -noauth, leave the username and password blank in step 3.

Note: imported rules become managed by Vauxtra: editing or deleting the service edits or deletes the Zoraxy rule. Creating a service for a hostname that already has a rule in Zoraxy is refused; import the rule instead.
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_2.title: Enter the Zoraxy URL
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_2.body: Enter the URL of the Zoraxy web console. The default port is 8000.
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_2.url.label: Zoraxy URL
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_2.url.hint: Use the internal IP or hostname. Include the port (default: 8000).
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_3.title: Zoraxy credentials
provider_guide.zoraxy.step_3.body: Enter the username and password of the Zoraxy web console. Leave both blank if Zoraxy runs with -noauth.
provider_guide.adguard.step_1.title: AdGuard Home connection details
provider_guide.adguard.step_1.body:
Vauxtra uses the AdGuard Home REST API with your web admin credentials.

No extra configuration is needed in AdGuard — just use the same username and password as the admin panel.

Default URL: http://<host>:3000
Default credentials set during first-run setup.
provider_guide.adguard.step_1.url.label: AdGuard URL
provider_guide.adguard.step_1.url.hint: Default port is 3000. Use the internal IP or hostname.
provider_guide.pihole.step_1.title: Find your Pi-hole API token
provider_guide.pihole.step_1.body:
Vauxtra uses the Pi-hole API to manage local DNS entries.

To find your API token:
  Pi-hole v5:  Settings → API / Web interface → Show API token
  Pi-hole v6:  Settings → API → Create / show API key

Alternatively, you can use your admin panel password directly.
The URL is typically http://<pi-hole-ip> (port 80, no /admin suffix).
provider_guide.pihole.step_2.title: Pi-hole URL and credentials
provider_guide.pihole.step_2.body: Enter the Pi-hole URL and the API token (or admin password) you located in the previous step.
provider_guide.pihole.step_2.url.label: Pi-hole URL
provider_guide.pihole.step_2.url.hint: IP or hostname only — no /admin suffix needed.
provider_guide.pihole.step_2.password.hi: Settings → API / Web interface → Show API token (v5) or Settings → API (v6).
provider_guide.traefik.step_1.title: Expose the Traefik API
provider_guide.traefik.step_1.body:
Vauxtra reads Traefik in read-only mode — it never modifies your routing configuration.

You need to expose the Traefik API on a reachable URL. Two common ways:

  Option A — Insecure (quick test):
    Add --api.insecure=true to your Traefik static config.
    API will be available at http://<host>:8080/api/

  Option B — Secure router (recommended):
    Create a dedicated Traefik entrypoint/router for /api/
    Add BasicAuth middleware if you want credentials.

Leave username/password blank if no auth is configured.
provider_guide.traefik.step_1.url.label: Traefik API URL
provider_guide.traefik.step_1.url.hint: Full URL to the Traefik API dashboard (no /api suffix needed).
provider_guide.cloudflare.step_1.title: Create a Cloudflare API Token
provider_guide.cloudflare.step_1.body:
Go to My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token.
Use the "Edit zone DNS" template, or a Custom Token with:
  • Zone → DNS → Edit (select your zone)

Copy the generated token and paste it below.
provider_guide.cloudflare.step_2.title: Zone ID (usually not needed)
provider_guide.cloudflare.step_2.body:
Your API token already defines which zones it can access.

Leave this blank unless you want to override the token scope.
Vauxtra will auto-detect zones from your token permissions.
provider_guide.cloudflare.step_2.usernam: Only needed if your token covers multiple zones and you want to restrict to one.
provider_guide.technitium.step_1.title: Prepare your DNS zones
provider_guide.technitium.step_1.body:
Vauxtra creates A records inside your existing Technitium zones.

Before connecting, you need at least one DNS zone set up in Technitium.

To create a zone:
  1. Open Technitium at http://<host>:5380
  2. Go to the Zones tab → Add Zone
  3. Choose Primary Zone, enter your domain (e.g. home.lab or home.local)
  4. Click Save

Vauxtra will auto-detect the correct zone for each service domain it manages.
provider_guide.technitium.step_2.title: Technitium credentials
provider_guide.technitium.step_2.body:
Enter the URL of your Technitium web console and your admin credentials.
Default port is 5380.
provider_guide.technitium.step_2.url.hin: Default port is 5380. Use the internal IP or hostname.
provider_guide.powerdns.step_1.title: Enable the PowerDNS HTTP API
provider_guide.powerdns.step_1.body:
The API is off by default. Add this to pdns.conf:

  api=yes
  api-key=<a long random string>
  webserver=yes
  webserver-address=0.0.0.0
  webserver-port=8081
  webserver-allow-from=<the IP running Vauxtra>/32

Restart pdns, then keep the API key — it is the only credential Vauxtra needs.

Keep webserver-allow-from as narrow as you can: anyone who reaches this API can rewrite every zone on the server.
provider_guide.powerdns.step_2.title: Create at least one zone
provider_guide.powerdns.step_2.body:
Vauxtra writes records inside zones PowerDNS already hosts. It never creates a zone.

  pdnsutil create-zone home.lab
  pdnsutil add-record home.lab @ A 3600 192.168.1.10

For each service hostname, Vauxtra picks the longest hosted zone that contains it.
provider_guide.powerdns.step_3.title: PowerDNS API details
provider_guide.powerdns.step_3.body:
Enter the address of the PowerDNS webserver and the API key you set above.

Leave the server id blank unless you changed it — almost every install answers to "localhost".
provider_guide.powerdns.step_3.url.label: PowerDNS API URL
provider_guide.powerdns.step_3.url.hint: The webserver address and port, without /api/v1.
provider_guide.desec.step_1.title: Register a domain with deSEC
provider_guide.desec.step_1.body:
deSEC is free, non-profit DNS hosting with DNSSEC on by default.

  1. Create an account at https://desec.io/
  2. Add your domain under Domain Management
  3. At your registrar, point the nameservers at deSEC:
       ns1.desec.io
       ns2.desec.org

A free dynDNS name under dedyn.io works too, and needs no registrar.

Vauxtra writes A, AAAA and CNAME records inside the domains this account holds.
provider_guide.desec.step_2.title: Create an API token
provider_guide.desec.step_2.body:
In the deSEC interface, open Token Management → Create Token.

Name it (e.g. "vauxtra") and leave the permissions alone — a plain token already reads and writes DNS records. Do not tick "Can manage tokens".

The token is shown once. Copy it now and paste it below.
provider_guide.desec.step_2.password.hin: Shown once, at creation. It grants write access to your DNS.
provider_guide.desec.step_3.title: Domain and endpoint (usually blank)
provider_guide.desec.step_3.body:
Leave both fields empty for the public deSEC service — Vauxtra detects your domains from the token itself.

Fill the domain in only to pin this provider to one domain when the account holds several. Fill the URL in only if you run your own deSEC stack.
provider_guide.desec.step_3.username.hin: Leave blank to use every domain the token can reach.
provider_guide.desec.step_3.url.label: API URL
provider_guide.desec.step_3.url.hint: Leave blank for the public service.
providers.type.desec.desc: Public DNS records via the deSEC API
Create a tunnel in Cloudflare Zero Trust

Go to dash.cloudflare.com → Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel.
Choose the Cloudflared connector type and give it a name (e.g. "homelab").

Vauxtra manages ingress routes inside the tunnel — it does not run cloudflared itself.
From the tunnel overview page, copy the Tunnel ID (UUID format). Paste it below.
Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → click your tunnel → Overview tab.
My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → Custom Token.
Required permissions:
  • Account → Cloudflare Tunnel → Edit
  • Zone → DNS → Edit (select your zone)

Copy the generated token and paste it below.
Never share this token — it grants Tunnel and DNS write access.
Your Account ID is a 32-character hex string shown in the right sidebar of dash.cloudflare.com (any zone overview page).
Right sidebar on dash.cloudflare.com → select any domain.
